checkpoint_review: The Router correctly identified that the silhouette nature of the image makes fine facial features (eyes, nostrils) and surface textures (color, denticles) untestable. It accurately marked these as N/A. The Router was correct to mark the cephalofoil shape, body streamlining, and fin structures as testable and present, as the silhouette clearly conveys the hammerhead's distinctive T-shape and heterocercal tail. I agree with all verdicts; no checkpoints were missed or misjudged.
artifact_review: The Router reported no artifacts. However, the perceptual_quality_auditor flagged a 'serious' level of darkening/underexposure (severity 0.8). While this is partly due to the underwater setting, the extreme darkness obscures significant detail, effectively acting as a visibility artifact. Additionally, the topology_boundary_auditor mask shows some fragmentation at the tail tip and dorsal fin edge, suggesting slight boundary instability common in low-contrast AI generations, though not catastrophic. The Router underestimated the impact of the lighting on evaluability, but strictly speaking, 'darkness' is an aesthetic/quality issue rather than a structural hallucination. I will penalize the artifact score slightly for the severe underexposure which degrades the image utility, but keep it relatively high as the subject remains recognizable.
